Chapter 3

Whenever Khaslana went through the next cycle with most of his morals and sanity strained and holding on by a thread, he would lay out the bare truth of his quest. Yes, he was going to take your coreflame; yes, he knows that you will never let it go without death; yes, he has done this x number of times; yes, he has 12x coreflames burning him from the inside out. No, he will not stop. No, he will not stop. No, he will not stop. (Yes, it hurt.)

This has perhaps led to an unfortunate habit: forgetting that his words, well-intentioned or not, would not disappear with death nor the next eternal recurrence.

In the changing rooms, he went to his knees.

"I am so sorry for the, uh," he struggled to remember the term he'd heard Stelle mention several times, "trauma dumping."

Both of them shared a look without saying anything at first, showing off the depth of a bond forged in fire and suffering.

"Go see a shrink." Was the advice Ratio gave before escaping into the showers.

Aventurine waved him off, "I see why Grammy's treatment would have that effect. It's no big deal."

"Have you ever gone back to her?"

"She said only to come back when I had a boyfriend as that would 'open up a whole different can of worms' apparently."

"Damn."

Phainon's master plan was going wonderfully, and if he were a bird, he'd practically be preening. Alas, confined to a human body and the expectations that came along with it, Phainon's smile stayed politely joyous until the cinema went black. Immediately, it twisted into a smile more suited for a fae waiting for disaster to strike.

He chose to sit two rows behind them, far enough to give the foretold illusion of privacy, but close enough to snoop. Ever since the movie started, Phainon ceased breathing for minimised presence.

As Stelle had informed Dan Heng, who had informed him, Aventurine was, indeed, unaffected by the gory slasher movie. Phainon squinted — indeed, his posture was actually even more relaxed than any other time during the vacation, potentially due to the morning's spa, but likely because he'd convinced Ratio to take his hand. Phainon nearly yelled from joy when Ratio accepted. Aventurine even took his gloves off for maximum skin contact — that man had game. It could have even been a rather obvious metaphor for something cooking between them (trust and vulnerability), but it was also flirty.

Phainon was impressed, mostly of himself for cooking up such a plan that minimised suffering. Even though Ratio tensed at nearly every jumpscare and blood-curdling scream, especially when he anticipated it, he didn't seem too scared. Hopefully.

But that was what the hero in shining armour, Aventurine himself, was for! At first, it was the hand holding, and then the blond's tactics escalated, soon leaning towards his crush during the more thrilling parts to perhaps create a very subtle physical barrier between them, and then Ratio leaned more to the left as the movie progressed. Aventurine's head was nearly on that man's shoulder! Phainon really was going to get a passing grade in matchmaking if things continued!!

As the main character dealt with the ethical dilemma of either cutting off the child's or the old man's legs to save their own lives, Phainon came to several epiphanies. (The first being that this particular movie's plot was also disappointingly simple, and the special effects also left a lot to be desired — such underwhelming arterial blood spray!)

Secondly, when Phainon the Dumbass of Cycle ??? invited Mydei to the movies, he shouldn't have placed himself in the role of the hero at all! No, what Phainon of Cycle 𝑥 should have been doing was playing the damsel! In extreme and implausible distress! He should have been leeching off of Mydei’s good graces by burrowing his face into that tattooed, delicious neck of his instead of even entertaining the silly, reckless plan of Mydei feeling even a shiver of adrenaline watching such a C-tier movie!

With a green face, he was miserably glad that his pawns had managed to score a good movie date.

"If you ever get too scared," he heard the low, soothing murmur of Aventurine’s voice, nigh indecipherable from the background wailing, "just look at me."

"Idiot." Ratio retorted, his face glowing red despite the awful lighting.

What had Phainon done? He was suffering from success. He was so damn envious he was going to throw up. Or even explode and take the whole planet down with him.

The climax of the film was steadily approaching. It was very obvious that the protagonist's homoerotic best friend was the villain mentally and psychologically torturing him behind an ugly mask.

Left in the back seats and being forced to watch as two maybe-lovers watched the other more than the movie made Phainon feel such a pang of sympathy for the lovely Castorice his stomach turned.

And then his brain, fully against both his will and expectations, began to connect the motherfucking dots. The third revelation held him hostage.

Her poetry book. His and Mydei’s names, over and over again. The chimerasonas that always held juuuuust a bit too much resemblance to the Chrysos Heirs. Castorice was the one who was always, always overcome with infectious joy when news broke out about his and Mydei’s updated relationship. Her attempts at matchmaking and peacemaking only made sense at that very moment, light years away from Amphoreus. Her three separate social media accounts, with the most secretive holding the most followers.

One time, they even wrote real person fanfiction together. It was Castorice who held the trigger and the pen and the lustrous prose together, deftly creating a mournful, yearning and corrosive epic of the Heretic and the Goldweaver. Phainon, out of drunken annoyance that he'd been held back a full decade from graduating; Castorice writing from the quiet joy of it.

The antagonist ripped off their ugly skull mask, revealing the bitch ass best friend's face underneath.

Phainon gasped in despair. "Oh Titans above!" He shouted.

GoldenHeretic was not Castorice's first rodeo into writing Chrysos Heir RPF.

In tandem with the protagonist, he despaired, "Oh, why, cruel world."

Somehow, over the course of 33 million epochs, he had never realised one of his best friends had been fujoshi-ing out (another Stelle Special) over him and Mydei. How had he been so damn blind?

In front of him, the hazy, romantic bubble between the destined couple broke.

"… Did he really not get that twist within the first five minutes?" Aventurine whispered, ears unnervingly close to the doctor's ear, who reflexively shivered.

"I believe he's going through a crisis unrelated to the movie." Ratio turned away first. Then, he nudged his head gingerly onto Aventurine’s soft hair, who stayed in place.

Aventurine smelled the faint apple scent of his doctor's shampoo, face brightening like a supernova, but his shoulders and neck as steady as time itself. Oh, Gaithra Triclops, thank the heavens for the dim lighting. His hands flexed, curling over Ratio’s just a tad harder. Still, neither of them pulled away for the duration of the movie.

Ratio did not flinch for the rest of the movie, even through the vengeance-fuelled montage of the protagonist beating their ex-situationship to death with a shovel.

Once the light finally dawned upon them again, it was clear that Phainon had gone through a most arduous moment of realisation, burdened by a most grim knowledge. Phainon ate the popped corn with morose disbelief. Aventurine reluctantly pulled away from his situationship before either of them had to face their unplatonic reactions..

"I think my friend has been writing poetry about me and Mydeimos since the very first cycle and I never realised. I'm a complete fool."

Ratio nodded in solemn agreement whilst Aventurine eyed the street for places to flee. (Ugh, maybe he shouldn't have invited him over to his actual apartment — he should've sent him to the summer house one two light centuries away.)

"How did I not notice?" Phainon whispered, eyes vacant.

Ratio glanced down at his watch, noting that he had a meeting in an hour. "By your reaction, it seems your friend's hobby was not particularly discreet. It's almost impressive that you missed being her muse for over 33 million lifetimes."

Phainon thought back to that dreadful cycle wherein he could no longer look his Professor in the eyes. Out of morbid curiosity, he asked, "Have you ever been…?" His sentence wandered off as his sanity flew back into him — there wasn't a good way to ask hey have you had raunchy smut written about you, nor was there any good reason why Phainon blurted it out. Damn, Phainon pre-massage would still have some semblance of social anxiety.

"One of my philosophy students accidentally sent in a 70,000 one-shot of myself in an ABO setting instead of their final assignment." His gaze went distant. "I ended up pulling an all-nighter to read it all. It was a most entertaining work of fiction and held fascinating insights into the problems of modern healthcare, with pre-existing concerns of bodily autonomy brought into another light due to the setting. Alas, she discontinued the series for 'personal reasons', and I believe it was because of that incident."

Phainon gaped — did the cosmos also have that accursed fictional trope?!

"… What is this 'ayy-bee-oh'?"

"You sweet summer child…" Phainon mourned.

They walked around the streets in only mildly awkward silence, a big step up from all of Phainon's other moments in creating an awkward atmosphere. His embarrassed state was soon drawn by a familiar, elusive and empty smile. In one of the many, many candy stores in Pier Point (allegedly it was an 'open secret' that some were just money laundering schemes) he saw a photo of Aventurine and his mildly smug, polite smile-smirk on display.

When he pointed it out, Aventurine laughed, face smoothing into the same smirk on display. "This store had a rather unique… fad that went viral a couple of years ago. I simply completed it and, ever since, my face has been on the wall of fame." For a moment, his smile transformed into a more mischievous grin that crinkled the corners of his eyes. His teeth flashed; Phainon felt a smidge of dread arise. "Wanna bring back some for your friends?"

Well, Tribbie and the others probably would like to try out some candy, especially Castorice and Mydei, who both had a sweet tooth one would usually find in a toddler.

And, well, his gifts were a bit underwhelming. He'd only brought those swanky fridge magnets, postcards, some snacks, clothes, jewellery (from both higher-end places and some from random stalls that were probably also money laundering schemes — but as Aventurine told him beforehand, they were really pretty. There were some thicker gold bracelets that would look great on Mydei, but then again, everything looked good on him—) and, finally, a really ugly cat statue for Anaxagorous or for Aglaea, depending on who would hate-love it more — yikes. Thinking about the list made him realise that he was definitely in debt to Aventurine. He didn't expect to become a sugar baby again.

"Sure!" Phainon managed to squeak out, still unsure whether Aventurine was lying when he said all those gifts were on him.

The lone salesperson perked up, not necessarily at the sight of new people to scam, but more so at the sight of the Aventurine Stoneheart. His portrait loomed over her like a herald of destruction wrapped in a glossy veneer, shiny eyes and shiny teeth sparkling.

"Are you here for a rematch?" She asked with a palpable reverence to the blond man beside him, the other two rendered unimportant.

Aventurine laughed smoothly and shook his head. "Ah, no, this is for my friend to try out." He gestured to Phainon; she looked at him as if he were a lamb ripe for the slaughter, pity in her eyes mixed with insatiable thirst for violence.

Once they made the purchase (she slipped to the back rooms and handed it off as discreetly as she could), Aventurine assured him, "There's no need for that look, mighty hero — besides, you'll be trying it out at my place."

Under the excuse of checking up on the 'little snack miscreants', Ratio finally allowed himself to be kidnapped for a proper sleepover. Phainon was amused to note that Aventurine already knew what the excuse was going to be, and that neither of the adult men before him had certainly ever had a sleepover before, much less with each other. That meant it was up to Phainon to act as the social lubricant of the night, of course, by using all of his previous experience to set up a sleepover that wouldn't end in disaster for their romantic prospects.

One thing that he hadn't accounted for was his non-existent, downright hostile baking skills. After the first time, even Hyacine barred him from entering her kitchen, and Little Ica would doot-doot with such forlorn misery whenever Phainon stepped a foot inside, even for a mere glass of water.

"Why didn't you preheat the oven?" He'd never heard Ratio so pissed before; now he fully understood why Stelle ran away from him in the train station. Aventurine, the lucky man on the sidelines, watched with mischievous glee. "Have you ever preheated an oven before? Phainon, answer me."

"Um." Phainon had to use all of his charisma currently available to avert the upcoming execution. May Castorice save him. "I-I've never preheated the oven."

At the resounding, loud silence, Phainon rushed to explain himself, "Honestly, I never thought people actually did that. Like putting in fabric softener into the laundry machine."

Ratio summoned chalk out of thin air, and Aventurine snickered with great amusement, big bug eyes taking in the show. "Minus points — get out of my kitchen."

With no more time left to squander, Phainon prostrated himself on the floor and did what he did best: talk, talk and talk.

"Have mercy, please! It's always been my beloved making meals for our friends and I to share and I thought to surprise him with a recipe from beyond the skies—"

"Cease your crocodile tears and rise." Ratio gave him a look that he'd seen on his old professor many times before, usually right before he sentenced Phainon to another year of failing his graduation, a look encompassed with disappointment and the desire to actually push their students beyond their limits. Man. He really should have listened to those instructions.

Ratio pulled up the recipe on his phone. "Alright then. We're starting with browning the butter."

Phainon squinted, damn well knowing that wasn't in the recipe.

"A beginner ought to follow the recipe to the letter," Ratio snapped.

"Browning butter is a technique used by many bakers to give their products a richer, nuttier flavour that enhances everything that needs butter, such as cookies and sauces. It is a result of the maillard reaction, which…"

Phainon focused on his words and the saucepan in front of him with the strained focus that carried him throughout his time in Amphoreus. The butter had already melted, the water slowly evaporating, and then the temperature of the milk solids began to increase drastically. Soon, the butter began to brown, as the name suggested, releasing a nutty aroma through the room. Was the temperature too high??

Ratio nodded in approval beside him, and the tremor in Phainon's hands finally receded.

"Why are you relaxing? We still have to combine the other ingredients, now get to it!"

"Yes, chef." Phainon received a swat on the arm for his response.

Phainon took another bite of the chocolate chip cookies that were so good even Idrilla THEMSELVES would weep in envy at their beauty. "Thank you," he croaked out, "is this the true dawn denied from my people.?

"How needlessly dramatic — it's just a cookie."

"No, Doc, they really are that good. I think Idrilla THEMSELVES must have blessed you and the cookies."

Ratio rolled his eyes, calling Aventurine a fool (affectionate) before ignoring everyone in the room to focus on the cat snack cat pet beings (?), stroking Poker's squishy case (torso??) until she all but melted into a little puddle of feline contentment. Phainon was betrayed by the sight — what did Ratio have that made all of the cats like him? Was it because Phainon had too much puppy energy?? Was Phainon just not good enough for those rascals???

Stewing in jealousy, he took another cookie, reclining back on the couch, which had a boxier look to it than anything out of Amphoreus, but it was so sinfully comfortable he could probably fall asleep on it.

"Have you guys ever had a sleepover before?" Phainon checked, and both confirmed they hadn't, which all lined up with his expectations. "Alright then. We will be building a blanket fort, then — if I allow both of you to go without this experience, I will have failed in my duty in being Okhema's Number One Blanket Fort Builder. Aventurine, do you have any extra blankets you could give out?"

"Sure?" Aventurine said, something in his voice suggesting he'd never constructed one before.

(Unbidden, he remembered that he was always in second place in that particular contest growing up — it was always more popular in Aedes Elysiae, where he was always beaten by Pito, the hunter's child.)

Through Phainon's expertise and Ratio's general knowledge, the fort went along swimmingly, especially as the blond brought some wine along with him. It was sharper and more bitter than the usual ceremonial wines Mydei, and by extension Phainon, drank. It wasn't bad at all.
